title: Building effective agents
author: Erik Schluntz and Barry Zhang, Anthropic (2024)
why: Defines workflows versus agents, catalogues the workflow patterns, and argues for the simplest design that works.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
author: Shunyu Yao et al. (2022)
why: The reasoning-action-observation loop that most agent frameworks still follow.

title: Tool use with Claude
author: Anthropic
why: A concrete reference for tool schemas, the tool_use stop reason and returning tool results and errors to the model.

title: The Anatomy of an Agent Harness
author: LangChain (2026)
why: Defines agent = model + harness and derives each harness part (tools, sandbox, memory, compaction, hooks) from what the model alone lacks.

title: Harness engineering for coding agent users
author: Birgitta Böckeler, martinfowler.com (2026)
why: Feedforward guides and feedback sensors (computational and inferential) that let a coding agent work with less supervision.

title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
author: Ryan Lopopolo, OpenAI (2026)
why: A team that shipped a product written entirely by agents, on making the repository legible to agents and enforcing architecture mechanically.

title: LangGraph Essentials (Python)
author: LangChain Academy
why: A free hands-on course on agents as explicit state graphs: nodes, edges, checkpoints and human interrupts.

title: LangChain Essentials (Python)
author: LangChain Academy
why: A free quickstart on models, tools and the basic tool-calling agent loop in LangChain.
